description: order.py's own 'triple-gate' re-check (DRY/EXEC/GATE, order.py:38-45) reads PM_PAPER_PASS from ITS OWN process environment via os.getenv, but run.sh never `export`s PM_PAPER_PASS before invoking order.py (run.sh:17-18 assign a plain, non-exported shell variable). Two failure modes follow: (a) if PM_PAPER_PASS is absent from the ambient/launchd environment (the realistic case, since it is purely computed inside run.sh from gate.py's stdout each run), order.py's own GATE will ALWAYS evaluate to os.getenv(None)=="1" -> False, so the intended real-order path can NEVER be reached through run.sh at all -- the 'wire the real executor' path in SKILL.md/run.sh is structurally dead code; or (b) if an operator statically sets PM_PAPER_PASS=1 in the launchd/cron environment (a plausible mistake given DRY_RUN/EARN_MODE ARE meant to be set that way), order.py's gate becomes a permanent rubber-stamp of a stale value completely decoupled from gate.py's live ledger computation -- reintroducing exactly the 'spoofable env var' vulnerability gate.py's own docstring (gate.py:2-6) claims was fixed (adversary FIND-004), just one layer lower. Either way, the documented 'all three gates must hold' safety property (order.py:2-5) is not actually true for the run.sh-driven code path as written.

evidence.snippet:
DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-true}"
EARN_MODE="${EARN_MODE:-observe}"
BANKROLL="${PM_BANKROLL:-8}"
GATE_OUT="$("$PY" "$HERE/gate.py" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
PM_PAPER_PASS="${GATE_OUT#PM_PAPER_PASS=}"; PM_PAPER_PASS="${PM_PAPER_PASS:-0}"
# ^ never exported; order.py (line 31) will not see this value in its own environ unless it was ALREADY an exported var before run.sh started.
